title: Smooth taxi/landings, IFR/VFR detection, category model matching, Zendriver FR24 fetch, optional native ATC
body:
## Description

Fixes the two main movement problems (taxi teleporting and runway overfly-then-teleport-into-taxi), improves IFR/VFR detection and model matching, replaces the FlightRadar24 data path with a Zendriver browser sidecar (the raw endpoints now block plain HTTP clients), and adds an opt-in path to hand aircraft to MSFS native ATC.

**Root causes found**
- Grounded aircraft were moved with `SetDataOnSimObject(PlaneLocation)` every ~10s — an instant teleport — and the ground waypoint was built from the *old* position with a hard-coded speed, so they jumped instead of driving.
- No real approach/landing transition: aircraft followed sparse 30s waypoints past the runway, then FR24 flipped `isGrounded=true` and the code teleported them onto a taxiway.
- The `OnGround` flag was inverted everywhere (`isGrounded ? 0 : 1`), so grounded aircraft were told they were airborne.
- No IFR/VFR detection at all; model matching defaulted every unmapped type to an A320 and could throw on short ICAO codes.
- The FR24 endpoints the app used are now blocked for plain HTTP clients: `data-live…/zones/fcgi/feed.js` → HTTP 302 and returns an empty stub even with cookies; `clickhandler` → HTTP 403.

**Changes**

*Taxi (smooth, no teleport)* — `LiveTrafficHandler.HandleGroundMovement`
- Track `lastSimLatitude/Longitude` and drive the AI to the new live point with an `ON_GROUND` waypoint at a realistic taxi speed (6–25 kts). Only re-sync (teleport) on first placement, right after touchdown, or when drift exceeds 120 m.

*Landing (no overfly, real rollout)* — `HandleAirborneMovement` + `IsOnApproach`
- Detect final approach and tighten the waypoint cadence to 8s (12s for GA, 30s for cruising airliners). On airborne→grounded, plant on the runway (`OnGround=1`) and roll out 250 m before switching to taxi. Fixed the inverted `OnGround` flag.

*IFR/VFR detection* — `Emum/FlightRule.cs`, `Util/FlightClassifier.cs`
- Heuristic classifier (scheduled airline / turbine on route / high cruise → IFR; light GA / glider / low-and-slow → VFR), surfaced as a **Rule** column.

*Model matching* — `Util/ModelMatching.cs`
- Null/empty-safe matching helpers and a `CategoryDefault(...)` (heavy → 747-8i, bizjet → CJ4, turboprop → Caravan, light → C172) instead of a universal A320 fallback.

*FlightRadar24 via Zendriver* — `fr24_fetcher.py`, `Util/Fr24Fetcher.cs`, `Util/ApiRequest.cs`, `Util/FlightRadarApi.cs`
- New Python sidecar `fr24_fetcher.py` drives a headless Chrome via Zendriver, warms up an authenticated `flightradar24.com` session, and serves a tiny localhost API: `GET /health` and `GET /fetch?url=<FR24 url>` (host-allowlisted). It fetches FR24 from inside the page (web-security disabled) so cross-origin calls to both `data-cloud` and `data-live` succeed.
- `Fr24Fetcher` (C#) launches/health-checks/stops the sidecar; `ApiRequest.MakeGetRequest` routes FR24 calls through it and **falls back to the direct HTTP path** if the sidecar is unavailable or returns non-JSON.
- Pointed the feed at the current host: `data-live` → `data-cloud` for `feed.js` (clickhandler stays on `data-live`).
- Config (`Settings`): `UseZendriver` (default **on**), `ZendriverPort` (8743), optional `PythonPath` / `ChromePath` overrides. Requires Python + `pip install -r requirements.txt` (Zendriver) + Chrome on the user's machine.

*Optional MSFS native ATC* — `Settings.UseNativeAtc` (default **off**), `Util/FlightPlanWriter.cs`
- Broadened eligibility: any flight (IFR **or** VFR, **departing or airborne**) with a known destination is created via `AICreateEnrouteATCAircraft` from a generated `.pln`; the plan's `<FPType>` is now set from the classifier (VFR/IFR) with a lower VFR cruise default. All other traffic stays client-driven.

## Review focus

- `Util/Fr24Fetcher.cs` lifecycle + the `ApiRequest` fallback: the sidecar adds a Python/Chrome runtime dependency. The feed (`data-cloud`) and clickhandler (`data-live`) routes were verified end-to-end through the running sidecar on the build VM (feed returned ~960 aircraft; clickhandler returned full aircraft detail). In-sim wiring (process launch on Connect, shutdown on Disconnect) is verified to compile only.
- `HandleGroundMovement` / `HandleAirborneMovement` thresholds (120 m drift, 250 m rollout, 8/12/30s cadence) want in-sim tuning.
- Native-ATC path is **experimental and opt-in**: FR24 gives no destination coordinates, so the `.pln` projects the destination ahead along the current track.

## Checklist

- [x] Solution builds cleanly (MSBuild + Roslyn toolset → `Enhanced Live Traffic.exe`)
- [x] Zendriver sidecar verified end-to-end on the build VM (feed + clickhandler over the localhost API)
- [ ] In-sim validation in MSFS2020 (no MSFS on the build machine)
- N/A `yarn format` / `yarn eslint` (C#/WPF project, no JS tooling)
- N/A changelog (repo has no CHANGELOG file)

## Screenshots or videos

<details>
<summary>Click to expand</summary>

No MSFS is available on the build VM, so in-sim behavior is verified to **compile** but not live-tested. The Zendriver FR24 fetch was live-verified on the VM. Recommend validating taxi smoothness, landing rollout, the IFR/VFR column, FR24 data flow with `UseZendriver`, and (if enabled) the native-ATC path in MSFS2020.

</details>
